title: Length of Last Word
description:
# Length of Last Word

Given a string `s` consisting of English letters and spaces, return the length of the **last word** in `s`.

A word is a continuous group of English letters separated by spaces or string boundaries. Leading, trailing, and intervening spaces are not part of a word.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "Hello World"
**Output:** 5
**Explanation:** The last word is `"World"`, whose length is 5.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "   fly me   to   the moon  "
**Output:** 4
**Explanation:** The last word is `"moon"`; leading, repeated, and trailing spaces are ignored.

## Example 3:

**Input:** s = "luffy is still joyboy"
**Output:** 6
**Explanation:** The last word is `"joyboy"`, whose length is 6.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= s.length <= 10^4`
* `s` consists only of English letters and spaces `' '`.
* `s` contains at least one word.

examples.input: s = "   fly me   to   the moon  "

solutions.name: Reverse Boundary Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach
Start at the end of the string. First skip all trailing spaces, because they are not part of the last word. Then keep moving left while the characters are non-spaces; the number of consumed characters is the answer.

## Key Insight
The last word is the final maximal non-space block before any trailing spaces. Scanning from the right reaches exactly that block without allocating substrings or arrays.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n), in the worst case the scan may inspect every character.
- Space Complexity: O(1), only indexes are stored.

solutions.name: Forward Word-Length State Machine
solutions.description:
## Approach
Scan from left to right. `current` counts the length of the word currently being read. When a space ends a word, store `current` as `last` and reset it. At the end, the answer is the active word length if the string ends in a word, otherwise the stored last length.

## Key Insight
This treats the string as a tiny state machine: inside a word or between words. It handles trailing spaces naturally because the most recently completed word is remembered.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n), every character is processed once.
- Space Complexity: O(1), only two counters are needed.

solutions.name: Trim and Last Space
solutions.description:
## Approach
Remove outer spaces with `trim`, then find the last remaining space. Everything after that space is the last word; if there is no space, the entire trimmed string is one word.

## Key Insight
This route converts the problem into a boundary-index calculation. It is concise and readable, but it may allocate a trimmed string, so it is less memory-efficient than the index-only scan.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n), trimming and searching each scan the string.
- Space Complexity: O(n), because `trim` can create a new string.

solutions.name: Regex Last Token Match
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use a regular expression to match the final non-space token and any trailing spaces at the end of the string. The length of the trimmed match is the length of the last word.

## Key Insight
The pattern describes the target directly: one or more non-space characters followed only by spaces until the end. This is a library-heavy route, useful for recognizing the problem as extracting the final token.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n), the matcher may scan across the input.
- Space Complexity: O(n), regex matching and trimming may allocate helper objects or strings.

solutions.name: Split Words Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach
Trim outer spaces, split the remaining string on one or more spaces, and return the length of the final array element. This follows the wording of the problem directly: turn the sentence into words, then inspect the last one.

## Key Insight
This is the simplest baseline for learners, but it does more work than necessary because it materializes every word even though only the last word is needed.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n), splitting scans the string.
- Space Complexity: O(n), the array and split substrings can use linear extra memory.
